result.topic_en: Euler decomposes the general term $\frac{1}{(x+a)^n x^m}$ of the double series $\sum \frac{1}{z^n}(1+\frac{1}{2^m}+\dots+\frac{1}{(z-1)^m})$ into partial fractions and begins summing the resulting terms by letting $a$ and $x$ run over all natural numbers.
result.transcription:
SERIES SINGVLARES. 169
modo autem in §. praec. vſitato $= q^n - p^{m+n}$; de
quo notetur eſſe per methodum primam
$q^m + q^n = p^m + p^{m+n} = p^n + p^{m+n}$ ob $p^m = p^n$.
Iam huius formae
$\frac{1}{z^n}\left(1 + \frac{1}{2^m} + \frac{1}{3^m} + \ldots\ldots + \frac{1}{(z-1)^m}\right)$
quilibet terminus continetur in hac forma $\frac{1}{(x+a)^n x^m}$
quae vti vidimus §. 6. reſoluitur in has partes:
$\frac{1}{a^n}\cdot\frac{1}{x^m} - \frac{n}{1\,a^{n+1}}\cdot\frac{1}{x^{m-1}} + \frac{n(n+1)}{1.2\,a^{n+2}}\cdot\frac{1}{x^{m-2}} - \frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{1.\ 2.\ 3\ a^{n+3}}\cdot\frac{1}{x^{m-3}}$ et
$\pm\frac{1}{a^m}\cdot\frac{1}{(a+x)^n} \pm \frac{m}{1\,a^{m+1}}\cdot\frac{1}{(x+a)^{n-1}} \pm \frac{m(m+1)}{1.2\,a^{m+2}}\cdot\frac{1}{(x+a)^{n-2}} \pm$ etc.
vbi ſignorum ambiguorum valent ſigna ſuperiora,
ſi $m$ eſt numerus par, inferiora vero ſi $m$ eſt nu-
merus impar; tum vero vtramque progreſſionem
eousque continuari conuenit, donec in ſuperiori fa-
ctoris $\frac{1}{x}$, in inferiori vero factoris $\frac{1}{x+a}$ exponens
euadat vnitas.

27. Vt igitur ſeriei propoſitae ſummam obti-
neamus, in formulae euolutae ſingulis terminis tam
loco $a$ quam loco $x$ omnes numeros naturali ordi-
ne progredientes ab vnitate in infinitum ſucceſſiue
ſcribi omnesque terminos inde oriundos in vnam
ſummam colligi oportet. Tum autem pro terminis
ſuperioris partis euolutae fore
$\int\frac{1}{a^n}\cdot\frac{1}{x^m} = \int\frac{1}{z^n}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^m} = p^n = p^m$

items.quote: $q^m + q^n = p^m + p^{m+n} = p^n + p^{m+n}$ ob $p^m = p^n$.
items.english: By the first method, $q^m + q^n = p^m + p^{m+n} = p^n + p^{m+n}$, because $p^m = p^n$.

items.quote:

items.english: Every term is contained in the form $\frac{1}{(x+a)^n x^m}$, which, as we saw in §. 6, resolves into these parts: (the stated expansion, with upper signs for even $m$ and lower signs for odd $m$).

items.quote:
Vt igitur ſeriei propoſitae ſummam obti-
neamus, in formulae euolutae ſingulis terminis tam
loco $a$ quam loco $x$ omnes numeros naturali ordi-
ne progredientes ab vnitate in infinitum ſucceſſiue
ſcribi omnesque terminos inde oriundos in vnam
ſummam colligi oportet.
items.english: To obtain the sum of the proposed series, in each term of the expanded formula all natural numbers from one to infinity must be substituted successively both for $a$ and for $x$, and all the resulting terms collected into one sum.
